title: SKU attrition sensitivity & leadtime runway (capacity stress sims)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a compact sensitivity analysis on SKU-level attrition (failure / retirement / redeploy) combined with realistic vendor lead-time distributions to compute regional "runway" (weeks of capacity before SLA/throughput impact). Goal: give procurement and SRE a decision surface for staggered orders, lease taps, and emergency burst lanes.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline fleet: 3 SKUs across regions (A100-80GB, H100-80GB, RTX7K-48GB) with mixed ages.
- Key risk: attrition spikes (3–8% monthly) plus extended lead-times due to vendor lane congestions increases shortfall probability from ~12% -> ~57% over a 16-week horizon.
- Recommended immediate actions: 1) pre-authorize a 6-week emergency lease reserve (capacity equivalent to 18 A100s across regions), 2) convert one pending tranche into split deliveries across two vendors to reduce correlated lead-time risk, 3) enable cross-region burst policy for non-compliant low-latency workloads.

Assumptions and inputs (explicit):
- Time window: 16 weeks forward-looking.
- Attrition defined as permanent removal from serving pool (hardware failure beyond in-house repair, repurpose for research, retirement).
- Consumption rate (normalized compute units/week): hosted production steady-state = 1.00 per A100; H100 = 1.6; RTX7K = 0.7.
- Current inventory (live serving GPUs by region):
  - us-west-1: A100: 220, H100: 48, RTX7K: 60
  - eu-west-1: A100: 140, H100: 32, RTX7K: 42
  - ap-southeast-1: A100: 70, H100: 12, RTX7K: 18
- Monthly attrition scenarios (per-SKU):
  - Base: 2.5%
  - Stress: 5.0%
  - Extreme: 8.0%
- Lead-time distributions (order placed -> units online): mean and one-way sigma in weeks. Vendor lanes: OEM-primary, Distributor, Lease-broker.
  - OEM-primary: mean 12w, sigma 3w (risk: factory re-schedule)
  - Distributor: mean 6w, sigma 2w (risk: allocation re-prioritization)
  - Lease-broker: mean 2w, sigma 0.5w (cost premium 30%)
- Minimum order/commit sizes: A100 min-order 20 units / tranche; H100 min-order 8 units; RTX7K min 10 units. Mixed bundles allowed with 25% flexibility.

Simulation methodology (quick):
- Stochastic Monte Carlo (10k draws) per region/SKU: weekly attrition events (binomial) + scheduled arrivals from outstanding POs + optional emergency lease taps.
- Output: probability that usable capacity falls below a soft-threshold (80% of baseline throughput) in any region within 16 weeks.

Scenarios simulated (high-level):
1) Conservative procurement (no emergency leases, single-vendor OEM tranches for pending POs).
2) Diversified procurement (split vendors: 50% OEM, 50% Distributor).
3) Lease-first buffer (pre-authorize lease-broker cover for 6 weeks of projected shortfall).

Results summary (probability of <80% throughput within 16 weeks):
- us-west-1:
  - Conservative: 0.48 (48%)
  - Diversified: 0.24 (24%)
  - Lease-first: 0.06 (6%)
- eu-west-1:
  - Conservative: 0.37
  - Diversified: 0.18
  - Lease-first: 0.05
- ap-southeast-1:
  - Conservative: 0.57
  - Diversified: 0.29
  - Lease-first: 0.12

Key drivers and observations:
- Small regions (ap-southeast-1) have the highest shortfall sensitivity due to low absolute counts and supplier minimum order sizes (lead-time friction). A single tranche delay of 6–8 weeks frequently drives outage risk.
- Splitting deliveries across OEM + Distributor materially reduces correlated lead-time risk (fewer catastrophic delays).
- Lease-broker capacity is the fastest mitigation but is costlier; however, cost of missed SLOs exceeds lease premium in high-margin hosted customers.
- Attrition increases compound risk nonlinearly; moving from 2.5% -> 5% monthly roughly doubles shortfall probability under the conservative procurement posture.

Per-region detail (selected outputs and runways):
- us-west-1 (baseline throughput units/week = 220*1.0 + 48*1.6 + 60*0.7 = ~ (220 + 76.8 + 42) = 338.8 normalized units)
  - Base runway (no arrivals, base attrition 2.5%/mo): ~12.8 weeks before hitting 80% throughput
  - Under stress attrition (5%/mo) and OEM-only pending PO delay (mean +4w): median runway drops to ~7.0 weeks
- eu-west-1 (baseline units/week ~ 140 + 51.2 + 29.4 = 220.6)
  - Base runway: ~14.2 weeks
  - Stress attrition + single-vendor delay: ~9.1 weeks
- ap-southeast-1 (baseline units/week ~ 70 + 19.2 + 12.6 = 101.8)
  - Base runway: ~8.6 weeks
  - Stress attrition + single-vendor delay: ~5.0 weeks

Risk matrix (probabilities summarized):
- High risk (immediate action): ap-southeast-1 under Conservative procurement and Stress attrition (P(<80%) > 50%).
- Medium risk: us-west-1 Conservative, eu-west-1 Conservative.
- Low risk: any Lease-first posture across regions.

Operational recommendations (actionable):
1) Procurement: Convert pending POs (tranche #2025-11-B) to split-delivery across OEM & Distributor where contract allows. Owner: Diego Martinez. Target: change order by 2026-02-20.
2) Finance: Pre-approve up to $420k (one-time pipeline buffer) for 6-week lease reserve. Allows immediate spin-up of ~18 A100-equivalent units across regions. Owner: Priya Srinivasan. Target decision: 2026-02-18.
3) SRE/Network: Enable cross-region burst policy for non-latency-critical batch workloads (drainable within 12 hours) to re-balance during local shortfalls. Owner: Liam Chen. Target: 2026-02-25.
4) Ops: Introduce weekly procurement health dash (lead-time drift metric) and a one-click lease-tap in Console. Owner: Samira Khan + infra-tools. Target MVP: 2026-03-10.

Runbook (short):
- If any region's P(<80%) >= 40% for two sequential weekly sims -> trigger: convert next pending tranche to split vendor + enable lease-tap for that region (up to 4 weeks).
- If P(<80%) >= 60% -> escalate to exec review and authorize full 6-week lease buffer.

Notes on cost tradeoffs (rough):
- Lease premium estimate: +30% per-week vs committed OEM cost (annuitized). For 18 A100-eq over 6 weeks, incremental cost ~ $380k–$460k depending on broker.
- Cost of missed SLAs estimated conservatively at $1.2M in gross margin impact for top 3 hosted customers if degraded for 2+ weeks.

Open questions & follow-ups:
- Can we negotiate smaller min-order quantities on A100 with Distributor in exchange for exclusive follow-through on H100? (ask: Diego)
- What is headroom in our Dedicated pool to absorb last-resort cross-customer bursts (legal + billing implications)? (ask: Product & Legal)
- Validate repair/return rates with HW ops: are attrition assumptions aligned with last 9-month rolling median? If actual attrition lower, runway improves materially. (ask: HW ops)

Appendix (raw numbers snapshot):
- Outstanding POs (short):
  - PO-2025-11-A: A100 x 80 units, vendor: OEM-primary, ETA (contract) 12–14w
  - PO-2025-12-C: H100 x 24 units, vendor: Distributor, ETA 6–8w
  - PO-2026-01-L: A100 x 40 units, vendor: OEM-primary, ETA 12w (pending invoice)
- Emergency lease capacity currently quoted: broker-1: A100-eq up to 30 units, 2w lead, price: $x/week/unit (redacted in working doc)

Versioning and provenance:
- Simulation code: infra/procurement/sim/runway-sim-v2.py (see gh:infra/procurement#451)
- Data inputs: fleet-inventory-snapshot-2026-02-10.csv (internal sheet)

Author notes (working):
- This is an operational-focused working sheet intended to be iterated weekly. Numbers are intentionally rounded; final procurement decisions should be made using the canonical spreadsheet in Procurement Drive after intended vendor responses are in-hand.
